 Follow Chloe Fineman Cast in New Comedy Movie That’s GTA VI Meets The Big Lebowski After SNL Exit
 Surya Singh Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:46 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: Hulu Chloe Fineman has landed her next film role following her departure from Saturday Night Live . She is set to star alongside Adam Devine in Miami PI , an independent crime comedy set against the backdrop of Miami Swim Week.
 According to Deadline , Michael Diliberti wrote the film and will direct it for Endurance Media. Production is scheduled to begin in March, with filming planned in Miami. The project is being offered to distributors at the upcoming American Film Market.
 The story follows a private investigator whose life has gone off track and a volatile former model who find themselves caught up in a murder investigation during the city's annual swim event.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As they dig deeper, the unlikely duo uncover a criminal conspiracy lurking beneath Miami's glamorous facade. Their partnership also develops into an attraction neither expected, adding another complication to the investigation.
 What else do we know about Chloe Fineman's new comedy movie?
 Miami PI is Diliberti's second feature as a director, following the 2025 action comedy Bad Man . That film starred Seann William Scott, Johnny Simmons , and Rob Riggle. Diliberti has also set up Worth, a detective drama in development at NBC, where he serves as writer and executive producer. The series follows decorated Army Ranger Will Worth as he returns to detective work in Nashville.
 Steve Richards will produce Miami PI for Endurance Media alongside Brian Levy of New School. Isaac Horne is attached as executive producer, with Jake Katofsky and Jake Neuberg also serving as producers. Thomas Sullivan will serve as the film's casting director. Endurance Media's recent production credits include Afterburn , The Killer's Game , and Freelance .
 Devine is best known for co-creating and starring in Comedy Central's hit series Workaholics and appearing across all four seasons of HBO's The Righteous Gemstones . His recent feature credits include Boots Riley's ensemble comedy I Love Boosters.
 Advertisement Advertisement Fineman joined Saturday Night Live in 2019 and became known for her celebrity impressions. She announced her departure in July 2026 after seven seasons on the NBC sketch show. Her upcoming projects include Netflix's Myron Bolitar , from David E. Kelley and Kyle Long, and Amazon's Red, White & Royal Wedding.
